checks.note: OAuth 2.0 with bot/user/app-level tokens and scopes confirmed on docs.slack.dev/authentication and /authentication/tokens. The Bearer header was not stated on the pages fetched. It is Slack's standard convention, but I did not verify it from a vendor page.

The cited changelog does not mention free workspace or app creation. A search of Slack docs says non-workflow custom apps can be developed on a Free plan, and automations need a paid plan. The Free plan's app cap is unconfirmed. The Developer Program sandbox is free but needs a payment method on file. The rate-limit changelog confirms the Marketplace caveat for commercially distributed apps. I kept self_serve_free, but the access evidence URL should be changed to a page that states free-plan app development.
The Web API has over 200 HTTP RPC methods. Socket Mode uses WebSockets (apps.connections.open). The WebSocket claim comes from the Socket Mode page, not the cited Web API page.
An official Slack MCP server is documented at docs.slack.dev with the endpoint https://mcp.slack.com/mcp. Only directory-published or internal apps are allowed, and workspace admins approve them.

ready_with_caveats fits. The blocker matches the changelog: Tier 1 (1 request/min) and a 15-object max on conversations.history and conversations.replies for non-Marketplace commercially distributed apps created on or after 2025-05-29. Internal apps are unaffected. The MCP restrictions are also confirmed.

corrected.one_liner: Slack is a workplace messaging platform with channels, DMs, files, and app integrations.
corrected.auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 (v2) yields bot (xoxb), user (xoxp), and app-level (xapp) tokens. Scopes are attached to tokens, and rotating tokens exist. Bearer-header transport is Slack's standard convention but was not confirmed on the vendor pages fetched. Requests from Slack are verified by signing secret (not fetched).
corrected.access_notes: Register apps at api.slack.com/apps. Slack's help docs say non-workflow custom apps can be developed on a Free plan, and automations need a paid plan. The Free plan's app-count cap was not confirmed for custom apps. The Developer Program sandbox is free but needs a payment method on file. Marketplace approval is needed to lift rate limits on commercially distributed apps. The MCP server requires a directory-published or internal app plus admin approval.
corrected.blocker: Commercially distributed apps outside the Marketplace (created on or after 2025-05-29, and new installs of older unlisted apps) are limited to Tier 1 (1 request/minute) on conversations.history and conversations.replies, with a maximum of 15 objects per request. Internal apps are unaffected. Marketplace approval removes the limit. The official MCP server only allows directory-published or internal apps, and admins must approve it.
